assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficient discrete-choice demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP), along with dynamic industry models, transformed empirical industrial organisation. It is now standard in merger review, antitrust and trade-policy evaluation, and in work on auctions, health and environmental economics. It is a methodological advance with very wide applied reach and demonstrated policy use.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes paper, together with Berry (1994), is the clear core. Pakes' further work on dynamic oligopoly (Ericson-Pakes) and on estimation adds to his share. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are important but more peripheral to the central demand-estimation breakthrough. Three laureates give a clean, defensible attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of use, replication and extension. The contribution has been thoroughly tested and its influence is not in doubt.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to include Bresnahan or the dynamic-games contributors.
Ranking relative to other methodological candidates is a judgement call.
Pakes' share could be argued to be larger than the other two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped trade theory and empirics. They moved the field from sector-level to firm-level analysis and changed how the gains from trade and the effects of trade policy are measured. Helpman's broader body of work on trade with imperfect competition and on firm-level integration choices adds depth.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central breakthrough. Helpman's contributions are numerous and foundational for the new trade theory and firm-level trade. Redding is highly influential on quantitative spatial and trade models, but his contribution is more downstream. The credited list omits other important contributors to firm-heterogeneity trade models, such as Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Yeaple. This weakens the claim of a clean attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of heavy empirical validation and extension. Krugman's earlier prize covered the preceding wave, so the firm-heterogeneity wave is plausibly ripe.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Yeaple, are not in the credited names.
Overlap with the Krugman prize may count against it.
Whether Redding should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and labour demand, together with the 'China shock' evidence on local labour-market adjustment, changed both academic and policy debate on inequality, automation and globalisation. The empirical designs are widely emulated and the results are policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work belongs mainly to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task framework builds on Autor-Levy-Murnane and Autor-Katz. Katz has a long record on skill-biased technical change but shares credit with others outside this list, including Acemoglu, Goldin and Murphy. Selecting Autor and Hanson is the tightest attribution, but it leaves out meaningful co-creators.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 20 years and is highly cited. Some lasting-effect claims remain contested, and later literature qualifies the magnitude of the trade-shock results.
uncertainties: Dorn and Katz are omitted from the proposal.
Robustness and interpretation of the China-shock estimates are still debated.
Overlap with the 2019 and 2021 empirical-labour prizes and with Acemoglu's 2024 award on technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) formalised the dynamic interaction between collateral constraints and asset prices, producing amplification and persistence in credit cycles. It is a foundation of modern macro-finance and was heavily used after the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint cycle model. Gertler is closely associated through the financial accelerator and later work, and Gilchrist through empirical tests, but both are less central. Bernanke's earlier prize covers the financial-accelerator tradition. This could dilute or complicate the claim.
assessment.maturity: Nearly 30 years old and well confirmed by theory and application. Quantitative evidence on how well collateral channels explain actual cycles is still mixed.
uncertainties: Whether Gertler should be included given his broader financial-frictions work.
Overlap with the 2022 banking prize and with Bernanke's earlier prize.
Empirical identification of collateral channels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Household-level evidence that credit-supply expansions and household leverage drove the housing boom and the depth of the Great Recession. It shifted macroeconomic and financial-stability thinking toward household balance sheets and credit-supply shocks, and it is empirically influential.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators of the empirical programme. Campbell's contributions lie mostly in asset pricing and household finance, so including him would blur the attribution.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of work. The core findings are widely replicated, but the long-run reception and theoretical consolidation are less complete than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Relative recency and whether the findings have been fully tested.
Debate over the interpretation of credit-supply versus expectations explanations for the boom.
Fit with the prior macro-finance recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, which pairs nominal rigidities and microfounded dynamic stochastic models with the theory and practice of monetary policy, is central to modern central-bank analysis. It is the workhorse of macroeconomic policy modelling.
assessment.attribution: This is a crowded field with many valid claimants: Calvo, Taylor, Gali, Woodford, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets. Any set of three leaves out major contributors, which weakens the attribution case. Woodford, Gali and Christiano combine theoretical foundations, the policy framework and the empirical medium-scale models, though this is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. It has been used in policy for decades and was tested by the financial crisis and by the post-pandemic inflation episode.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely difficult, with eight credited names and no unique trio.
Taylor, Calvo and Eichenbaum are plausible alternatives.
The framework's forecasting failures during and after the crisis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research established that legal origin and investor protection are associated with financial development and corporate ownership structure. It opened a large cross-country empirical literature and affected institutional and policy debates. Its significance is high, but the causal interpretation of legal origins has been challenged on identification grounds.
assessment.attribution: The La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny papers (1997-2008) form a coherent group. Shleifer's work in behavioural finance and corporate governance goes well beyond this group. Credit attribution is clear within the group, though Vishny's inclusion is arguable. As a corporate-finance researcher I note proximity to my own field, and that proximity is not evidence of merit.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of heavy citation. The empirical debate over measurement of legal-origin variables and their causal role remains open, and this lowers the confidence about how durable the central claims are.
uncertainties: Causal identification of legal origins and critiques of the shareholder-protection indices.
Whether the Committee would credit the research agenda rather than a settled discovery.
Reputational controversies around individual candidates, which are not scientific merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring misallocation of inputs across firms (Hsieh-Klenow 2009) offered a quantitative account of cross-country income and TFP differences. It has had substantial influence on growth and development economics, with wide empirical application and policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the authors of the central empirical framework. Restuccia and Rogerson have a parallel and slightly earlier theoretical contribution, but Rogerson is not on the credited list, which makes a three-person attribution awkward. The measurement approach also depends on strong structural assumptions.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years old with extensive application. Concerns about measurement error and about what the dispersion of marginal products actually reveals temper confidence.
uncertainties: Measurement-error critiques of the misallocation estimates.
Rogerson's omission from the credited names.
Ranking against more established methodological and theoretical contributions.
